stem:
A gardener in Murree planted the same variety of tomato in two beds. One bed received full sun all day; the other was shaded by a wall after noon. Both beds were watered and fed in exactly the same way. By the end of summer, the sunny bed had produced twice as much fruit, which suggests that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the wall had released chemicals into the soil of the shaded bed.
the shaded bed must have been given less water than the sunny bed.
this tomato variety grows best when it is shaded for most of the day.
the extra sunlight was probably responsible for the larger harvest.
explanation: Water and feeding were identical, so the main remaining difference is sunlight. The water option contradicts 'watered and fed in exactly the same way'.

stem:
Glass frogs of Central America have almost see-through skin on their bellies. Biologists found that when a glass frog sleeps on a leaf, it pulls most of its red blood cells into its liver, which is covered by a reflective layer. Because blood is the most visible part of a resting frog's body, this behaviour probably ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: helps the frog digest food more quickly while it is asleep.
allows the frog to change the colour of the leaf it rests on.
makes the sleeping frog much harder for predators to spot.
lets the frog breathe through its skin while it is underwater.
explanation: If blood is the most visible part and the frog hides it in a reflective organ, the frog becomes harder to see. Nothing in the text concerns digestion or breathing underwater.

stem:
In the 1800s, the British East India Company kept careful records of the price of grain in district markets. Historian Kamran Iqbal noticed that in several famine years, grain prices in some districts barely rose even though harvests had failed. Since a shortage normally pushes prices up, Iqbal concluded that in those districts ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the Company had stopped keeping records of prices in district markets.
grain was probably arriving from elsewhere to make up for the failed harvests.
the harvests had in fact been much larger than the official records showed.
people had stopped eating grain altogether during the famine years.
explanation: Prices stay level during a local harvest failure if supply comes from outside. The option that harvests were larger contradicts 'harvests had failed', which Iqbal takes as given.

stem:
Mahnoor's class planted beans in two trays. The first tray was kept in a warm room and the second in a cold storeroom. The beans in the warm room sprouted in four days, but those in the storeroom took more than two weeks. Mahnoor concluded that, for these beans, ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: cold air stops all growth.
warmth speeds up sprouting.
trays slow down sprouting.
light is needed to sprout.
explanation: The only stated difference is temperature, and the warm tray sprouted faster. The cold beans did eventually sprout, so 'stops all growth' is too strong, and light was never tested.

stem:
Most reviews of the novelist's early books praised their humour, and her publisher marketed them as comedies. Her later books, which dealt with grief and illness, sold far fewer copies, even though critics now rate them as her best. One literary historian argues that readers who had come to expect comedy from her ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: probably bought the later books in larger numbers than the earlier comedies.
may have been put off by the change in tone rather than by the quality of the writing.
must have agreed with critics that the later books were her finest achievements.
were mainly responsible for the publisher's decision to market the books as comedies.
explanation: The historian is explaining weak sales of highly rated books; a mismatch with readers' expectations explains why good books sold poorly. The option saying sales were larger contradicts 'sold far fewer copies'.

stem:
Engineers testing a new road surface in Sukkur poured two stretches side by side, one with the standard mix and one with a mix containing recycled plastic. After two hot summers, the standard stretch had developed deep ruts where heavy trucks braked, while the plastic stretch showed only shallow marks. If the traffic on both stretches was the same, the results suggest that the plastic mix ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: resists softening and rutting under heat and heavy loads better than the standard mix.
was poured more carefully than the standard mix by the construction team.
should be replaced with the standard mix on roads that carry heavy trucks.
was used by fewer heavy trucks than the stretch built with the standard mix.
explanation: With equal traffic, the shallower marks point to the plastic mix holding up better. The fewer-trucks option contradicts the condition that traffic was the same.

stem:
Owls can turn their heads about 270 degrees, much farther than most birds. Unlike human eyes, an owl's eyes are fixed in place and cannot move in their sockets. Turning the head so far therefore allows owls to ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: look around them even though their eyes cannot move.
fly faster than birds that cannot turn their heads.
hear sounds coming from far beneath the ground.
see colours that most other birds cannot detect.
explanation: Because the eyes are fixed, owls must move their heads to change where they look. Colour vision, speed and hearing are not linked to head turning in the text.

stem:
A clothing brand in Lahore launched the same shirt online in two versions of its website. The first version showed only photographs of the shirt; the second added short videos of people wearing it. Both versions had the same price and appeared for the same number of days, yet the version with videos sold almost twice as many shirts. This result suggests that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: shoppers were attracted mainly by a lower price on the second website.
the photographs on the first website were of poor quality and unclear.
seeing the shirt being worn made shoppers more willing to buy it.
most shoppers prefer to buy shirts in shops rather than on the internet.
explanation: Price and time were equal, so the added videos are the likely cause. The lower-price option contradicts 'the same price'.

stem:
Astronomers measuring a distant star found that its brightness dips by the same small amount every 12 days, and each dip lasts about three hours. A planet crossing in front of a star blocks some of its light in exactly this regular way, but so can a dark spot on a spinning star. Since starspots usually change size and fade over a few weeks, the fact that the dips have stayed identical for two years suggests that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the star's light has been growing steadily brighter over two years.
the star spins once every three hours rather than every 12 days.
a large starspot has remained exactly the same size for two years.
a planet orbiting the star is the more likely cause of the dips.
explanation: Starspots change within weeks, while the dips stayed identical for two years, which favours a planet. The starspot option asks us to accept exactly what the text says starspots do not usually do.

stem:
In many Pakistani cities, rooftop water tanks are black plastic. Tahira, an engineering student, measured water temperature in black and white tanks on the same roof. On summer afternoons the water in the black tank was up to 12 °C warmer. For households that want cool water in summer, her results imply that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: tank colour makes no difference at all.
water should be stored only at night.
black tanks should be filled more often.
white tanks would be the better choice.
explanation: Black tanks heated the water up to 12 °C more, so white tanks keep water cooler. The no-difference option contradicts her measurements.

stem:
Ali noticed that the bread he bought from a bakery stayed soft for a week, while the bread he baked at home went stale in two days. He used flour, water, yeast and salt. The label on the bakery bread listed those four ingredients plus a preservative. A likely reason the bakery bread lasted longer is that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the bakery used much less salt than Ali used at home.
it contained a preservative that Ali's bread lacked.
Ali's flour had come from a different kind of wheat.
the bakery baked its bread at a lower temperature.
explanation: The only listed difference in ingredients is the preservative. Flour type, salt amount and temperature are not mentioned, so those options rely on information the text does not give.

stem:
Linguists studying a remote valley in Chitral found that older speakers used separate words for 'snow that is falling', 'snow on the ground' and 'snow hard enough to walk on', while younger speakers who had moved to towns used a single word for all three. The researchers suggested that the older vocabulary survives mainly where ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: towns receive more snowfall than the high villages of the valley.
older speakers have stopped using their language in daily life.
younger speakers have never learned any words at all for snow.
people's daily lives still depend on telling these kinds of snow apart.
explanation: The split falls between valley life and town life, so the distinctions likely last where they still matter in daily life. The option that younger speakers know no words contradicts the statement that they use a single word.

stem:
Coral reefs get their bright colours from tiny algae that live inside the coral and provide it with food. When sea water becomes too warm, the coral expels these algae and turns white, a process called bleaching. If the water cools again soon enough, the algae can return. A reef that stays white for many months is therefore likely to ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: have grown much faster than reefs that kept their algae.
be in water that has cooled down quickly after a heatwave.
contain more algae than usual inside its white coral.
be starving, since it has lost the algae that feed it.
explanation: The algae supply the coral's food, so long bleaching means long loss of food. The cooled-water option contradicts the idea that algae return when water cools soon.

stem:
For centuries, the main ports of the Indian Ocean traded according to the monsoon winds, which blow from the southwest for part of the year and from the northeast for the rest. A merchant sailing from Arabia to India had to wait months for the winds to change before returning. This pattern meant that many merchants ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: preferred to travel overland instead of crossing the ocean.
spent long periods living in foreign port towns between voyages.
sailed only during calm periods when there was no wind at all.
could make several round trips between Arabia and India each month.
explanation: Waiting months for the winds to change before the return voyage meant long stays abroad. Several round trips a month is impossible if each return requires a seasonal wind change.

stem:
Some birds, such as swallows, leave Europe each autumn and fly to Africa. Insects, which swallows eat, become scarce in European winters but remain plentiful in parts of Africa. This suggests that swallows migrate mainly to ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: find enough food during winter.
avoid flying in strong winds.
build nests in a warmer place.
escape birds that hunt them.
explanation: The text links migration to insects, the swallows' food, being scarce in Europe and plentiful in Africa. Predators, nests and winds are not mentioned.

stem:
A pharmaceutical company reported that patients who took its new sleep medicine slept, on average, 30 minutes longer than before. An independent researcher pointed out that the study had no comparison group: all participants took the medicine, and all knew they were taking it. Since people who expect to sleep better often do, the 30-minute gain ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: may not show how much of the improvement the medicine itself caused.
would have been larger if the patients had not known about the medicine.
proves that the medicine works better than any other sleep treatment.
shows that the patients slept less than they had before the study.
explanation: Without a comparison group, expectation alone could explain the gain, so the medicine's own effect is unclear. The option about knowing the medicine assumes the opposite of the expectation effect the researcher describes.

stem:
Cities that build new roads to reduce traffic jams often find that, within a few years, the new roads are just as crowded. Planners call this 'induced demand': when driving becomes easier, people make trips they once avoided or chose to make by bus. Given this pattern, adding lanes to a busy road is unlikely to ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: change how many cars use it.
attract any new drivers to it.
solve its traffic jams for long.
cost the city any money at all.
explanation: Induced demand means extra lanes fill with new trips, so jams return. The other options contradict the idea that easier driving draws more cars.

stem:
Saima's grandmother keeps her rice in a sealed tin. Her neighbour stores rice in an open sack. Every few months, the neighbour finds small insects in her rice, while Saima's grandmother never has. This suggests that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the grandmother's rice is a different colour.
the neighbour's rice is cooked more often.
the sealed tin keeps insects out of the rice.
insects prefer sacks to rice inside tins.
explanation: Only the open sack lets insects reach the rice, so the seal is the likely reason. The text says nothing about rice colour or cooking.

stem:
Researchers studying Pakistani university students found that those who studied in short sessions spread over several days remembered more material a month later than those who studied the same total hours in one long session the night before a test. However, the two groups scored the same on a test given the morning after studying. This suggests that spreading out study mainly helps with ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: studying for longer each night of the week.
finishing the reading in fewer total hours.
remembering material over the longer term.
scoring well on tests the very next day.
explanation: Next-morning scores were equal, but spaced study won a month later, so its advantage is long-term memory. The next-day option contradicts the equal morning scores.

stem:
Early maps of the Arabian Sea coast drawn by Portuguese sailors show the mouth of the Indus at a point now many kilometres from the sea. Geologists have found layers of river mud stretching seaward from that point. Taken together, the maps and the mud layers suggest that over the past few centuries ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the river has stopped carrying any mud down from the mountains.
the river has built up new land and pushed the coast outward.
the Portuguese sailors drew their maps without visiting the coast.
the sea has risen and covered land that once lay near the river.
explanation: The old mouth now lies far inland, and river mud extends seaward, so the delta has grown. The rising-sea option would move the coast inland, not seaward.

stem:
Dolphins in a marine park learned to trade rubbish that fell into their pool for fish from their trainers. One dolphin began hiding a sheet of paper under a rock and tearing off small pieces, bringing them up one at a time. Since each piece earned a fish, this behaviour suggests the dolphin had learned that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: several small pieces would earn more fish than one large sheet.
the trainers would refuse any paper that was hidden under rocks.
rubbish was dangerous and needed to be hidden from other dolphins.
large pieces of paper earned more fish than small pieces did.
explanation: If each piece earns a fish, tearing the sheet multiplies the rewards. The last option contradicts the dolphin's choice to tear the paper into small pieces.

stem:
Mountains of the Himalaya are still rising by a few millimetres each year, because the plate carrying India continues to push north into Asia. If this movement continues, the height of these mountains is likely to ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: change only when it rains heavily.
keep increasing slowly over time.
stay exactly the same for centuries.
fall quickly in the next few years.
explanation: The mountains rise as the plate keeps pushing, so continued movement means continued slow growth. 'Stay exactly the same' contradicts the stated annual rise.

stem:
A survey of farmers in Sindh found that those who owned their land were much more likely to plant trees along field edges than those who rented land on one-year contracts. Trees take several years to grow before they give fruit, shade or timber. A likely explanation for the difference is that renters ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: had more time than landowners to look after young trees properly.
earned far more from their crops than the farmers who owned their land.
preferred to plant trees in the middle of their fields instead of the edges.
could not be sure they would still farm the land when the trees matured.
explanation: On one-year contracts, renters may lose the land before trees pay off. The middle-of-field option invents a preference the survey did not report.

stem:
Some historians credit the spread of tea drinking in South Asia mainly to advertising campaigns of the 1930s. Yet tea sales in the region grew fastest in the 1950s and 1960s, decades in which advertising spending on tea was falling. Economist Laila Farooq notes that these decades also saw rapid growth in railway travel, with tea sold at every station. Her observation suggests that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: advertising campaigns of the 1930s were the main cause of tea's popularity.
tea sales fell sharply in the decades when railway travel was growing.
railway passengers in the region refused to drink tea sold at stations.
railway stations may have done more than advertising to spread the habit.
explanation: Sales rose fastest when advertising fell but railways, with tea at every station, grew, pointing to the railways. The advertising option is the view her evidence challenges.

stem:
Usman's phone battery used to last a full day. After he installed a new game that keeps running in the background, the battery began running out by early afternoon. Usman made no other changes to his phone. The new game is probably ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: using a lot of the battery's power.
making the screen less bright.
protecting the battery from damage.
charging the battery more slowly.
explanation: The only change was a game that runs in the background, and the battery now drains sooner. A dimmer screen would save power, not use it.

stem:
In medieval Europe, books were copied by hand, often by monks, and a single copy could take months. When printing presses arrived in the fifteenth century, the price of books fell sharply. Historians have found that, in the decades that followed, far more ordinary merchants and craftsmen owned books than before. This suggests that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: lower prices helped bring books within reach of more people.
printed books took longer to make than books copied by hand.
monks stopped reading books once printing presses were invented.
merchants had always owned more books than monks had owned.
explanation: Prices fell and then ownership spread to merchants and craftsmen, linking cheaper books to wider ownership. The option about printing taking longer contradicts the falling price and faster copying.

stem:
Moths are attracted to lights at night, and street lamps can draw thousands of them away from the plants they would normally pollinate. Researchers in one town replaced white street lamps with amber ones, which give off very little of the light that moths are most drawn to. Over the next summer, they would expect ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: moths in the town to stop flying at night completely.
more moths to be drawn to the town's new street lamps.
fewer moths to gather around the town's street lamps.
plants in the town to need no pollination by moths at all.
explanation: Amber lamps give little of the light moths prefer, so fewer moths should be drawn to them. The option about more moths reverses that reasoning.

stem:
Ice floats on water because it is less dense than liquid water. In winter, a lake freezes from the top down, and the layer of ice on its surface acts like a lid that slows further heat loss. As a result, the water beneath the ice usually ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: sinks below the bed of the lake until the spring.
stays liquid, allowing fish to survive the winter.
freezes solid long before the surface does.
becomes much warmer than it is in the summer months.
explanation: The floating ice insulates the water below, so it stays liquid. Freezing from the bottom first contradicts 'freezes from the top down'.

stem:
A school in Gilgit switched its morning tea for students from sweetened milk tea to plain milk. Teachers recorded fewer students complaining of tiredness before lunch. However, during the same term the school also moved its sports period from the afternoon to the early morning. Because both changes happened together, the teachers cannot yet say whether ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the change of drink was the reason students felt less tired.
students in Gilgit preferred plain milk to sweetened milk tea.
the students had complained of tiredness before lunch at all.
the sports period had been held in the afternoon in earlier years.
explanation: Two changes at once mean either could explain the result, so the drink's role is uncertain. The afternoon sports period is stated in the text, so there is no doubt about it.

stem:
Nineteenth-century travellers often described the city of Thatta as nearly deserted, and historians long took these accounts as proof that its trade had collapsed. A recent study of customs records, however, shows a steady flow of cotton and indigo through Thatta's markets in the same decades. The travellers mostly visited in the hot season, when merchants left for the hills. This suggests that the travellers' accounts ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: may reflect the season of their visits more than the state of the city's trade.
prove that Thatta's merchants had moved away from the city permanently.
were written by people who had never actually been to the city of Thatta.
show that customs records from the period cannot be trusted by historians.
explanation: Customs records show ongoing trade, and the visitors came when merchants were away, so the emptiness may be seasonal. 'Permanently' contradicts the point that merchants returned from the hills.

stem:
Plants growing on windy hillsides are often shorter and have thicker stems than the same species growing in sheltered valleys. In an experiment, researchers gently shook young plants for a few seconds every day indoors, with no wind at all. The shaken plants also grew shorter and thicker than unshaken ones. This suggests that the plants ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: need strong wind in order to grow thicker stems than usual.
respond to being moved, not to some other feature of windy places.
grow shorter only when they are planted on high, cold hillsides.
were damaged by the shaking and could not grow to normal height.
explanation: Shaking alone, without wind, cold or altitude, produced the same form, so movement itself is the trigger. The cold-hillside option ignores that the indoor plants changed too.

stem:
Bilal's small shop sells ice cream and hot pakoras. He has noticed that on hot days he sells far more ice cream, while on cold, rainy days pakoras sell best. If the weather forecast says next week will be cold and wet, Bilal should probably ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: prepare more pakoras than ice cream.
lower the price of every pakora.
close the shop because no one will come.
order extra ice cream for the week.
explanation: Cold, rainy days favour pakoras, so he should stock more of them. Closing the shop ignores that pakoras sell best in exactly that weather.

stem:
In a study of language learners, one group practised new Arabic words by writing them out by hand, while another typed them on laptops. Both groups spent the same amount of time. A week later, the handwriting group recalled more of the words. The researchers suggested that the slower, more effortful act of forming each letter ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: caused the handwriting group to forget words more quickly.
may have helped the learners fix the words in memory.
prevented the handwriting group from finishing the word list.
made the learners spend less time on each word than typists did.
explanation: Equal time but better recall points to the effort of handwriting aiding memory. The forgetting option contradicts the handwriting group recalling more.

stem:
The economist found that in towns where a new factory opened, wages in nearby shops and restaurants also rose within two years, even though those businesses did not hire factory workers. She argues that the factory raised wages indirectly: because it offered better pay, shop owners ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: lowered prices to attract the factory's workers as their customers.
had to raise their own wages to keep staff from leaving for factory jobs.
hired factory workers to work in their shops during the evenings.
were required by the factory to pay their staff the same wages.
explanation: An indirect effect through competition for workers means shops matched pay to keep staff. Hiring factory workers contradicts the statement that shops did not hire them.

stem:
Many deep-sea fish produce their own light, a trait called bioluminescence. Sunlight does not reach the deep ocean, where it is completely dark. For these fish, making light is useful because otherwise ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: they could see almost nothing around them.
they would not need to find any food.
they would be too warm in the cold water.
they would swim too close to the surface.
explanation: With no sunlight in the deep ocean, a fish without its own light would be in total darkness. The text does not link light to temperature or depth.

stem:
Archaeologists working in Balochistan found grains of wheat and barley in layers of a settlement dated to about 7000 BCE. Wild forms of these plants do not grow in the area today, and no wild grains were found in the older layers below. The finds suggest that the early settlers ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: gathered the wheat and barley from wild plants growing nearby.
did not eat bread or any other food made from grain at all.
brought cultivated crops with them or learned of them from elsewhere.
abandoned the settlement before the grains had been planted.
explanation: With no wild grains nearby or in earlier layers, the crops probably came already domesticated. Gathering from nearby wild plants contradicts the lack of wild forms.

stem:
The poet often revised her poems for years before publishing them, and her notebooks show dozens of versions of some lines. When a collection of her earliest drafts was published after her death, some readers were surprised by how plain and direct the first versions were. The drafts suggest that the rich, layered style for which she is known ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: was abandoned by the poet late in her writing career.
was already present in the first versions she wrote down.
came from her editor, who rewrote the poems after her death.
developed largely through her long process of revision.
explanation: Plain first drafts and many revisions show the style grew through rewriting. Saying the style was present from the first versions contradicts the readers' surprise at their plainness.

stem:
A coffee shop in Islamabad stopped giving out free plastic straws and began offering them only when customers asked. Before the change, the shop used about 500 straws a day. Most customers never asked for one after the change, so the shop probably ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: began to charge customers for their coffee.
ran out of straws within the first week.
used more straws than before the change.
began using far fewer straws each day.
explanation: If most customers no longer took straws, daily use fell well below 500. Running out of straws would require higher use, not lower.

stem:
In laboratory tests, a new antibiotic killed every strain of a bacterium it was tested against. Yet doctors warn against using it widely at first. Bacteria that survive a drug, they note, can pass on their resistance as they multiply, and the more often a drug is used, the more chances resistant bacteria have to appear. Keeping the new drug for the hardest cases is therefore meant to ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: make sure that the drug reaches as many patients as possible quickly.
test whether the drug can kill strains that it has already killed.
slow the spread of resistance so that the drug stays useful longer.
allow bacteria to become resistant to the drug as fast as possible.
explanation: Wider use gives resistance more chances to arise, so limiting use protects the drug. Reaching as many patients as possible quickly is the opposite of the doctors' advice.

stem:
In 2015 a city in Punjab painted bright zebra crossings near schools and added signs telling drivers to slow down. A year later, records showed the same number of accidents near schools as before. Officials then installed speed bumps at the same crossings, and accidents fell by half in the following year. This suggests that drivers ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: had always driven slowly near schools before 2015 anyway.
slowed down more for physical barriers than for paint and signs.
could not see the zebra crossings because they were too bright.
drove faster near schools after the speed bumps were installed.
explanation: Paint and signs left accidents unchanged, while speed bumps halved them, so physical barriers changed driving more. Faster driving after the bumps would not fit fewer accidents.

stem:
Earthworms dig tunnels through soil as they feed. These tunnels let air and rainwater move down to plant roots. A gardener who finds many earthworms in her soil can therefore expect that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: water and air reach her plants' roots easily.
her plants are being eaten by the worms.
the soil is too hard for roots to grow.
her plants will need no water at all.
explanation: The tunnels carry air and water to roots, so many worms mean good access. Hard soil contradicts the loosening effect of their tunnels.

stem:
Historians have long wondered why a medieval trading town on the Arabian Sea was suddenly abandoned. Sediment cores from the harbour show that, around the time the town emptied, thick layers of sand began building up across the harbour mouth within a few decades. For a town that depended on ships, this change probably ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: had no effect on trade because goods arrived over land.
made the town's harbour deeper and much safer for ships.
made it hard or impossible for ships to reach its harbour.
allowed larger ships than before to dock in the harbour.
explanation: Sand building up at the harbour mouth would block ships, explaining abandonment by a shipping town. A deeper harbour reverses the effect of sand piling up.

stem:
Research on reading has found that children who are read to at home often know many more words when they start school. A charity in Hyderabad gave free picture books to families with young children, but a year later the children's vocabularies had grown no more than those of other children. Interviews revealed that most parents had put the books away to keep them clean. The results suggest that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: picture books are less useful for learning than books without pictures.
owning books helps vocabulary only if the books are actually read.
children in Hyderabad already knew more words than other children.
reading to children at home has no effect on the words they learn.
explanation: The books did not help because they were not read, so use, not ownership, matters. The last option contradicts the research the text opens with.

stem:
A study found that people who own dogs are, on average, more physically active than people who do not. Some concluded that getting a dog makes people more active. But psychologist Nida Karim points out that active people may be more likely to choose a dog in the first place. To test whether dogs really cause the difference, researchers would need to ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: ask dog owners whether they believe their dogs make them more active.
measure how active dogs are when their owners are away at work.
count how many dogs are owned by the most active people in a city.
compare people's activity levels before and after they get a dog.
explanation: Karim's concern is that activity might come first; tracking the same people before and after getting a dog separates cause from choice. Counting dogs among active people repeats the original correlation.

stem:
In Pakistan, wheat is usually sown in November and harvested in April or May. Rice, on the other hand, is sown in early summer and harvested in autumn. This means that a farmer who grows both crops on the same field ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: must harvest both crops at the same time.
can grow only one crop in any single year.
needs to sow both crops in the month of May.
can plant one crop after harvesting the other.
explanation: Wheat is harvested by May and rice is sown in early summer, so the seasons fit one after the other. The other options contradict the different sowing and harvest months.

stem:
Bats that hunt insects send out high-pitched calls and listen for echoes. Some moths can hear these calls. When a moth detects a bat's call nearby, it often folds its wings and drops towards the ground. This behaviour probably helps the moth ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: catch insects that are flying close to the ground.
escape the bat by suddenly changing its path.
attract other moths that can warn it of danger.
make its own calls louder than the bat's.
explanation: Dropping abruptly when a bat is heard is an escape move. Nothing suggests moths call, hunt insects or warn each other.

stem:
A survey of 3,000 households in Karachi found that those living within a short walk of a public park reported more weekly exercise than households farther away. The researchers then checked households that had moved: families who moved closer to a park began exercising more, while those who moved farther away exercised less. These later findings strengthen the idea that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: parks in Karachi are used mainly by people who live far away.
people who like exercise always choose to live near parks.
moving house makes people exercise less, whatever the location.
being near a park itself encourages people to exercise.
explanation: Exercise changed with distance for the same families after moving, pointing to parks having an effect. The option that moving always reduces exercise contradicts families who moved closer exercising more.

stem:
For decades, scientists thought that giant pandas were solitary animals that met only to mate. Collars that recorded the positions of several pandas in China's Sichuan forests showed that some pandas' ranges overlapped widely, and that pairs of pandas sometimes spent weeks in the same small area outside the mating season. These data suggest that panda social life ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: has remained exactly as scientists described it before.
consists of large herds that travel together all year.
is limited strictly to the weeks of the mating season.
may be more complex than the earlier view allowed.
explanation: Pandas sharing space for weeks outside mating season challenges the 'solitary' view without proving herd life. The herd option overstates what tracking a few pairs shows.

stem:
A new bridge in a town near Peshawar cut the trip across the river from forty minutes by ferry to five minutes by car. Within a year, the number of ferry passengers had fallen sharply. This was probably because ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the river had become too wide for ferries.
the bridge was closed for most of the year.
many travellers chose the faster bridge.
ferry tickets had become much cheaper.
explanation: A trip eight times faster explains the drop in ferry passengers. Cheaper ferry tickets would attract passengers, not lose them.

stem:
The ancient city of Petra, in present-day Jordan, lay in a dry region with little rain. Archaeologists have found channels cut into the rock, dams across narrow valleys and large underground tanks throughout the city. These structures suggest that the people of Petra ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: lived mainly by fishing in rivers near the city.
used the tanks only to store grain for the winter.
worked hard to collect and store scarce water.
built their city where rain fell almost every day.
explanation: In a dry region, channels, dams and tanks point to managing water. The daily-rain option contradicts 'little rain'.

stem:
A software firm let half its staff choose their own working hours, while the other half kept a fixed 9-to-5 schedule. After six months, the two groups completed the same amount of work, but the flexible group took fewer sick days and reported less stress. If the firm's main aim is to keep its staff healthy without losing output, the results suggest it should ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: require the flexible group to work longer hours each day.
reduce the amount of work given to the flexible group.
return all employees to fixed hours to raise their output.
consider offering flexible hours to more of its employees.
explanation: Flexible hours kept output equal while improving health, matching the firm's aim. Returning to fixed hours to raise output ignores that output was already equal.

stem:
The historian notes that the oldest surviving copies of a famous medieval poem all come from monasteries in one region, and that each contains the same unusual spelling mistakes. Copies from other regions, made later, correct these mistakes but keep the same line order. She concludes that the later copies were probably ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: produced by scribes who had never seen any earlier copy.
copied from a completely different version of the poem.
made from copies descended from the monastery versions.
written by the original poet before the monastery copies.
explanation: Later copies share the monastery copies' line order and fix their particular mistakes, suggesting they descend from them. A completely different source would not be expected to share the same line order and signs of those errors.

stem:
Lemons, limes and oranges contain a lot of vitamin C. In the past, sailors on long voyages often became ill with scurvy, a disease caused by lack of vitamin C. When ships began carrying citrus fruit for the crew, cases of scurvy ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: became much less common.
spread to people on land.
became far more common.
stayed exactly the same.
explanation: Scurvy comes from lacking vitamin C, and citrus supplies it, so cases fell. 'More common' reverses the cause.

stem:
A team studying air quality in Lahore placed sensors both indoors and outdoors in 50 homes. On smoggy winter days, indoor pollution in most homes was nearly as high as outdoor pollution. Homes with tightly sealed windows and air filters, however, had far lower indoor levels. This suggests that, on smoggy days, staying inside ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: is always much safer than spending time outdoors in the city.
has no effect on how much pollution people breathe at all.
protects people only if outside air is kept out or filtered.
makes indoor air more polluted than the air outside the home.
explanation: Most homes were nearly as polluted as outdoors, but sealed, filtered homes were cleaner, so indoors helps only with those measures. 'Always much safer' ignores the many homes where it did not help.

stem:
Snow reflects most of the sunlight that falls on it, while dark rock and soil absorb much more. As snow on a mountain melts in spring, more dark ground is exposed. The exposed ground therefore ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: absorbs more heat, which can speed up further melting.
keeps the mountain colder than it was in winter.
reflects even more sunlight than the snow had reflected before.
stops the sun from reaching the remaining snow on the slopes.
explanation: Dark ground absorbs more sunlight, so it warms and can melt nearby snow faster. Reflecting more than snow contradicts the first sentence.

stem:
A bookshop in Lahore moved its poetry shelves from a back corner to a table near the entrance. Over the next three months, poetry sales tripled, although the shop stocked the same titles at the same prices. The owner concluded that many customers ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: were willing to pay much higher prices for books of poetry.
preferred novels to poetry and avoided the table near the entrance.
bought poetry only when it was placed in the back corner.
had not bought poetry before simply because they had not noticed it.
explanation: Titles and prices were unchanged; only visibility changed, and sales tripled. The higher-price option contradicts 'the same prices'.

stem:
Climate records show that the city's average summer temperature rose by 1.5 °C over forty years. Over the same period, the city grew rapidly, replacing fields with concrete and asphalt, which store heat. A weather station in farmland 60 kilometres away recorded a rise of only 0.5 °C. Together these records suggest that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the weather station out in the farmland must have been measuring the temperature incorrectly all along.
much of the city's warming may come from its own growth rather than wider climate change.
the farmland around the city warmed faster than the city itself did during those years.
the city's temperature would have fallen if no concrete or asphalt had been laid.
explanation: The countryside warmed by 0.5 °C, the growing city by 1.5 °C, so the extra 1 °C likely comes from urban heat storage. The 'would have fallen' option overreaches, since the farmland also warmed.

stem:
Bees from a hive kept near a field of sunflowers made honey with a light, golden colour. When the same hive was moved near a forest of acacia trees the following year, the honey turned almost clear. The beekeeper's methods did not change. The difference in colour was most likely caused by ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the different flowers from which the bees collected nectar.
a change in the way the beekeeper collected the honey.
the hive producing more honey near the sunflower field.
the bees working much harder in the forest than in the field.
explanation: Only the location and so the nectar source changed, so the flowers explain the colour. A change in the beekeeper's methods contradicts 'did not change'.

stem:
Many cats dislike getting wet, but the Turkish Van breed often swims in lakes and pools. Its coat has a texture that repels water, so it dries quickly. This suggests that the Turkish Van's coat ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: makes swimming more comfortable for it.
keeps it from going near water for long.
becomes heavy and soaked when it swims.
prevents it from catching any fish at all.
explanation: A water-repelling coat that dries fast suits a cat that swims. 'Heavy and soaked' contradicts the coat repelling water.

stem:
In one study, workers at a call centre were asked to rate how happy they felt each morning. On mornings when they reported being happier, they made more sales that day. The researchers caution that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: successful days might themselves have followed from something that also lifted mood.
the workers had made no sales at all on any of the mornings in the study.
the workers had not been asked to rate their happiness each morning.
happier workers always make more sales in every kind of job.
explanation: A link between mood and sales does not show that mood caused sales; a third factor could affect both. 'Always ... in every kind of job' is the kind of overreach the caution warns against.

stem:
The writer Intizar Husain often set stories in the small towns of his childhood, and his later works return again and again to the events of 1947, when he moved from India to Pakistan. Critics note that his memories of the town he left are vivid but his descriptions of Lahore, where he lived for decades, are sparse. This suggests that, as a writer, Husain was drawn mainly to ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: events that took place long after 1947 in Lahore.
stories set in countries he had never visited.
the places and times he had lost.
the modern life of the city of Lahore.
explanation: His fiction keeps returning to childhood towns and 1947, while Lahore receives little description. The Lahore options contradict the 'sparse' treatment of the city.

stem:
Bird-watchers in the Margalla Hills counted more species of birds in 2023 than in 2003. Some concluded that the forest had become healthier. But the number of bird-watchers taking part had also risen sharply, and many newcomers used phone apps that help identify rare species. Before concluding that the forest is healthier, researchers would need to know whether ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the bird-watchers who took part in 2003 also lived in or near the city of Islamabad at the time.
the higher count reflects more birds or simply more and better-equipped observers.
the forest had any birds living in it at all during 2003.
the phone apps used by the bird-watchers cost money to download.
explanation: More observers with better tools could raise the count even if bird life stayed the same, so that must be ruled out. Where watchers lived or app prices do not bear on that question.

stem:
Kiwi birds of New Zealand cannot fly. For millions of years, before people arrived, New Zealand had no land mammals that hunted birds. Without such predators, the kiwi's ancestors probably ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: lived only on islands far from land.
had little need to escape by flying.
were hunted by many land mammals.
had to fly to find food every day.
explanation: With no ground predators, flying away was less necessary, making flightlessness possible. 'Hunted by many land mammals' contradicts the text.

stem:
For years, a textile mill in Faisalabad dumped coloured wastewater into a nearby canal. After the mill installed a treatment plant, villagers downstream reported that fish had returned to the canal. No other factories discharge into that stretch of water. The return of the fish is therefore most likely due to ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: other factories that closed along the canal.
villagers releasing fish raised in their ponds.
an increase in the colour of the canal water.
the cleaner water now leaving the mill.
explanation: No other factories use that stretch, so the mill's treated water is the likely cause. The closed-factories option contradicts 'No other factories discharge'.

stem:
Scientists studying chimpanzees in Guinea found that the animals use stones to crack nuts, and that young chimpanzees take several years to master the technique. Young chimps watched their mothers closely and often used stones their mothers had just set down. These observations suggest that the skill ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: appears fully formed as soon as a young chimpanzee can hold a stone.
is no longer used by the chimpanzees that live in Guinea.
is passed on largely by watching and copying older chimpanzees.
is learned from chimpanzees in other groups rather than from mothers.
explanation: Years of learning while watching mothers and using their stones point to social learning. 'Fully formed' contradicts the several years needed to master it.

stem:
An economist tracking rice prices noticed that when the government announced it would buy large amounts of rice for storage, market prices often rose before any rice had actually been bought. She explained that traders, expecting prices to rise once the government began buying, ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: lowered their prices to attract more customers before the purchases began.
bought rice from the government's stores to sell in their own shops.
held back their own stock, which reduced supply in the market straight away.
sold all their rice at once to the government at below-market prices.
explanation: Prices rose before any purchase, which fits traders withholding supply in anticipation. Lowering prices or selling everything would push prices down, not up.

stem:
Some plants close their flowers at night and open them again in the morning. A student put one such plant in a dark cupboard during the day, and the flowers closed within an hour. When she brought it back into the light, they opened again. This suggests that the flowers respond mainly to ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: light rather than the time of day.
the temperature of the soil.
the time of day rather than light.
how often the plant is watered.
explanation: The flowers closed in darkness at midday and reopened in light, so light, not the clock, controls them. The time-of-day option is the idea the experiment rules out.

stem:
Bridges made of steel expand on hot days and contract on cold days. Engineers leave small gaps, called expansion joints, between sections of a long bridge. Without these gaps, the sections would ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: push against each other in heat and could crack or buckle.
stop expanding on hot days and contracting on cold days.
rust much more slowly than sections that are separated by joints.
become lighter and easier for heavy vehicles to cross.
explanation: Expanding sections need room; without gaps they would press together and could damage the bridge. Steel still expands with heat, joints or not, so the second option is wrong.

stem:
A museum in Karachi tried two versions of a label for a 4,000-year-old clay pot. One gave only the pot's age and place of discovery; the other added a short story about the family who might have used it. Visitors spent, on average, twice as long at the pot with the story label. The museum might reasonably conclude that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: visitors prefer clay pots to any other kind of object.
longer labels always make visitors leave a museum sooner.
human stories can increase visitors' interest in objects.
the age of an object no longer interests museum visitors.
explanation: The story label doubled viewing time, suggesting narrative draws interest. The claim that age no longer interests visitors goes far beyond the comparison, since both labels gave the age.

stem:
Medical records from a hospital in Multan show that patients admitted at night stayed, on average, a day longer than patients admitted during the day. One doctor suggested that night-time care was worse. Another pointed out that patients arriving at night were more often emergency cases with serious injuries. The second doctor's point implies that the longer stays ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: would disappear if the hospital closed its doors to patients at night.
were caused by patients choosing to arrive at the hospital at night.
prove that night-time staff at the hospital were poorly trained for their work.
might reflect how ill the patients were rather than the quality of night-time care.
explanation: If night patients were sicker on arrival, their longer stays need not reflect poorer care. The 'prove ... poorly trained' option repeats the first doctor's claim that the second doctor questions.

stem:
Raza wanted to know whether his new running shoes made him faster. He ran the same 5-kilometre route in old shoes on Monday and new shoes on Tuesday. On Tuesday it rained heavily, and he ran more slowly. Because the weather was different, Raza cannot be sure that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: he ran the same route on both days.
he wore old shoes on Monday.
it rained on Tuesday during his run.
the shoes caused the change in his time.
explanation: Rain is a second difference that could explain the slower time, so the shoes' effect is unclear. The rain, route and shoes are all stated facts, not doubts.

stem:
Early telescopes produced images with coloured fringes because lenses bend different colours of light by different amounts. In the 1660s, Isaac Newton built a telescope that used a curved mirror instead of a lens to collect light. Since a mirror reflects all colours in the same way, Newton's design ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: avoided the coloured fringes that troubled lens telescopes.
made the coloured fringes around bright objects even wider than before.
needed several additional lenses to work correctly.
could be used only to look at very bright stars.
explanation: Mirrors treat all colours alike, so they do not split colours into fringes. Wider fringes reverse the point of the design.

stem:
In a village near Swat, most families once grew their own vegetables. After a paved road connected the village to a market town, many families stopped growing vegetables and planted fruit trees instead, selling the fruit in town. This change suggests that the road ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: caused the soil around the village to become unsuitable for vegetables.
reduced the number of people from the village who chose to visit the market town each week.
made it worthwhile to grow crops for sale rather than only for home use.
made it impossible to buy vegetables in the village or in the town.
explanation: Families switched to fruit sold in town once the road arrived, so market access changed what was worth growing. The soil option offers a cause the text gives no evidence for.

stem:
Seeds of many desert plants can lie in dry soil for years without sprouting. They sprout quickly after heavy rain, grow, flower and make new seeds within a few weeks. This pattern helps the plants ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: avoid flowering after it has rained.
survive in places with daily rain.
make the most of rare periods of water.
grow tall during long dry seasons.
explanation: Rapid growth after rare rain lets the plants complete their life cycle while water lasts. 'Avoid flowering after rain' contradicts the text.

stem:
A study compared students in schools that banned phones during the school day with students in schools that allowed them. Students in the ban schools scored higher on exams. However, the ban schools were also, on average, better funded and had smaller classes. To show that the ban itself raised scores, researchers would ideally compare ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: students' opinions of the phone ban with their teachers' opinions of it.
schools that are alike in funding and class size but differ in their phone rules.
the exam scores of students who own their own phones with those of students who own laptops instead.
the best-funded schools with the worst-funded schools, ignoring phone rules.
explanation: Funding and class size are rival explanations, so schools matched on those but differing in phone rules isolate the ban. Comparing best- and worst-funded schools tests funding, not the ban.

stem:
The Thar Desert receives most of its rain in a few weeks of the monsoon. Traditional houses in the region often have thick mud walls and small windows. Thick mud walls absorb heat slowly during the day and release it slowly at night. These features probably help the houses ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: dry out quickly after the monsoon rains.
stay cooler by day and warmer by night.
let in more sunlight during the summer.
collect rainwater for the long dry months.
explanation: Walls that take in and give out heat slowly smooth out the daily swing in temperature. Small windows reduce sunlight, so 'let in more sunlight' is the opposite.

stem:
When Sadia's family switched from incandescent bulbs to LED bulbs, their electricity bill fell noticeably, even though they used their lights for the same number of hours. LED bulbs give the same light while using much less electricity. The fall in the bill therefore probably came from ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: leaving the lights on for fewer hours.
the lower energy use of the new bulbs.
a rise in the price of each unit of power.
buying more lamps for their home.
explanation: Hours were unchanged, and LEDs use much less power, so the bulbs explain the saving. Fewer hours contradicts 'the same number of hours'; a price rise would raise the bill.

stem:
Woodpeckers hammer their beaks against tree trunks many times a second to find insects and dig nest holes. Their skulls contain spongy bone that absorbs shock. Without this spongy bone, woodpeckers would probably ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: build their nests on the ground.
stop eating insects found in trees.
risk injuring their heads while pecking.
peck much faster than they do now.
explanation: The bone absorbs shock from hammering, so without it the head would suffer more force. Pecking faster is not linked to losing shock absorption.

stem:
For many years, a small airline flew between Islamabad and Skardu only in good weather, because pilots had to see the mountains to land safely. After the airport installed modern navigation equipment that guides planes in poor visibility, the number of cancelled flights fell sharply. This suggests that most earlier cancellations were caused by ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: a lack of passengers wishing to fly to Skardu.
pilots refusing to fly to airports with new equipment.
the high price of fuel for flights into the mountains.
weather that made it hard for pilots to see.
explanation: Equipment that helps in poor visibility cut cancellations, so poor visibility caused most of them. Fuel prices and passenger numbers are not affected by navigation equipment.

stem:
Historians long held that a medieval sultan built a canal mainly to irrigate farmland. Excavations show that the canal ran past the sultan's hunting grounds and gardens but bypassed the largest farming villages nearby. Court poems of the time praise the canal's fountains, never its harvests. This evidence suggests that the canal ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: carried water to the sultan's hunting grounds but never to his gardens.
was built only after the farming villages had been abandoned by farmers.
was the main source of water for the largest farming villages nearby.
may have been intended more for royal pleasure than for agriculture.
explanation: The route served royal grounds and gardens and skipped farms, and poems praised fountains, pointing to pleasure over irrigation. The first option contradicts the canal bypassing the largest villages.

stem:
Hamza left a bowl of water on a sunny windowsill and an identical bowl in a dark cupboard. After three days, the bowl on the windowsill held much less water. Since the room was the same temperature throughout, the sunlight probably ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: made the water much colder than before.
made the water evaporate faster.
stopped the water in the cupboard from evaporating at all.
added more water to the bowl on the sill.
explanation: The sunny bowl lost more water, so sunlight likely sped evaporation. 'Added more water' contradicts the bowl holding less.

stem:
Researchers found that shoppers in a Karachi supermarket bought more fruit when it was placed near the entrance than when it was at the back of the store. Prices and types of fruit were the same in both cases. This suggests that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: shoppers were attracted mainly by lower prices near the entrance.
where products are placed can affect what shoppers buy.
fruit at the back of the store was of much poorer quality than usual.
shoppers in Karachi do not usually buy any fruit in supermarkets.
explanation: With price and type unchanged, location is the difference that changed sales. The lower-price option contradicts 'Prices ... were the same'.

stem:
Polar bears have black skin under their thick white fur. Black surfaces absorb heat from sunlight well. This feature probably helps polar bears ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: hide from the sun during the summer.
cool down quickly when they swim in icy water.
see better during the long Arctic nights.
stay warm in their cold surroundings.
explanation: Black skin absorbs heat, which helps an animal in a cold place stay warm. Cooling down is the opposite effect.

stem:
Historians studying a nineteenth-century trading family in Peshawar found letters written in Persian, Pashto, Urdu and English. Letters to partners in Central Asia were mostly in Persian, while those to British officials were in English. This suggests that the family ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: kept letters in many languages only as a hobby, not for business.
chose the language of each letter to suit the person receiving it.
traded only with partners who lived in the city of Peshawar itself.
wrote in Persian only because they could not read or write in English.
explanation: The language matched the recipient, Persian for Central Asia and English for British officials. The option about not knowing English contradicts the English letters they wrote.

stem:
A new phone app claims to improve memory. In a trial, 200 users played its games daily for a month and then scored higher on the app's own memory games. They did not score higher on other memory tests that used different kinds of tasks. The results suggest that the app's users ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: mostly became better at the app's games rather than at remembering in general.
improved their memory for every type of task they were tested on afterwards.
played the app's games less often than the trial's instructions required.
scored lower on the app's games after a month of daily practice.
explanation: Gains appeared only on the practised games, not on other memory tests, so the skill did not transfer. The 'every type of task' option contradicts the flat scores on other tests.

stem:
In some parts of the Himalayas, villagers build 'ice stupas', tall cones of frozen water made in winter by spraying water into freezing air. Because a cone has less surface exposed to the sun than a flat sheet of ice of the same volume, the stupas ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: can be built only during the hot summer months.
melt slowly and can supply water well into spring.
are made from river water that never freezes in winter.
melt faster than flat ice and are gone by midwinter.
explanation: Less surface exposed to sunlight means slower melting, keeping water stored longer. Faster melting reverses the reasoning about surface area.

stem:
Amna's tea always went cold quickly in a thin glass cup. When she started using a thick clay mug, her tea stayed hot for much longer. The thick mug probably ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: lets heat escape much more quickly than thin glass.
lets heat escape more slowly.
makes the tea itself hotter.
changes the taste of the tea.
explanation: Tea stayed hot longer, so the thick mug must slow heat loss. 'Escape more quickly' is the opposite.

stem:
When a dam was built upstream of a delta, the river began carrying much less sand and mud to the sea. Over the following decades, parts of the delta's coastline began to wash away. This suggests that the delta ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: was protected from waves by the new dam built far upstream.
had grown much larger in the years after the dam was built upstream.
had never received any sand or mud from the river before the dam.
had depended on river sediment to replace land worn away by the sea.
explanation: Less sediment followed by coastal loss means the delta needed river sediment to keep up with erosion. 'Never received any sand' contradicts the river once carrying more.

stem:
Two schools taught the same maths course. School A's students scored higher on the final exam. School A, however, admitted students only after an entrance test, while School B admitted anyone who applied. Before concluding that School A teaches maths better, one would need to know ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: whether School A's buildings were newer than School B's buildings.
how many students at School B enjoyed the maths course they took.
how the two groups of students compared before the course began.
how many teachers in each school had studied maths at university.
explanation: The entrance test may have given School A stronger students from the start, so starting levels must be compared. Enjoyment or buildings do not address that selection problem.

stem:
Cactuses store water in their thick stems. Their sharp spines protect these stems from animals. In a dry desert, where water is scarce, the spines probably stop animals from ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: eating the stems to get water.
digging up the cactus seeds.
sleeping in the shade of the cactus during hot days.
drinking from nearby desert streams.
explanation: Water-filled stems would attract thirsty animals, and spines protect them. The text never mentions streams, shade or seeds.

stem:
A teacher noticed that her students answered more questions correctly when tests were held in the morning than in the afternoon. She then moved the afternoon class's test to the morning, and that class's scores rose to match. This suggests that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the teacher had made the morning test much easier than before.
students always score worse in the morning than in the afternoon.
the time of the test, not the class, explained the difference.
the afternoon class had weaker students than the morning class did.
explanation: Once the afternoon class tested in the morning, its scores rose to match, so timing was the cause. The weaker-students option is ruled out by that rise.

stem:
In ancient Egypt, farmers depended on the yearly flooding of the Nile, which left a layer of rich mud on their fields. Records show that in years when the flood was unusually low, food prices rose. This suggests that low floods ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: had no effect on the crops that farmers grew in Egypt.
left less fertile mud and led to smaller harvests.
caused farmers to stop paying their taxes to the pharaoh.
made the fields far more fertile than in normal years.
explanation: Less flooding meant less mud and smaller harvests, so prices rose. More fertile fields would lower prices, not raise them.

stem:
Owais planted sunflowers along a wall on the east side of his garden. Over the summer, he saw the flower heads face east each morning. Sunflowers are known to follow the sun. In the morning, the sun must be ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: low in the western sky.
hidden behind the clouds.
in the eastern sky.
directly overhead.
explanation: Flowers that follow the sun and face east in the morning show the sun is in the east then. The western sky is where it sets.

stem:
A city introduced a fee for cars entering its centre. Traffic in the centre fell by a fifth, but traffic on the ring road around the centre rose by almost the same number of cars. City planners realised that the fee had mostly ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: caused traffic in the city centre to rise by about a fifth.
had no effect at all on how many cars entered the centre.
persuaded drivers to sell their cars and travel only by bicycle.
moved traffic to other roads rather than reducing total driving.
explanation: The fall in the centre was matched by a rise on the ring road, so cars shifted rather than disappeared. 'No effect' contradicts the drop of a fifth.

stem:
Students at a Lahore college were offered a free snack if they took the stairs instead of the lift. Use of the stairs rose sharply while the offer lasted. A month after the offer ended, stair use had dropped back to its earlier level. This suggests that the offer ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: reduced the number of students who used the stairs.
did not create a lasting habit of using the stairs.
made the lift slower than before for all students.
made students use the stairs permanently after it ended.
explanation: Stair use fell back once the offer ended, so no lasting habit formed. 'Permanently' contradicts the return to the earlier level.

stem:
Leaves of many trees in Islamabad turn yellow and fall in autumn. During winter, there is less sunlight and the ground can freeze, making it hard for roots to take up water. Dropping leaves probably helps the trees ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: catch more sunlight in the cold months.
make new seeds in the cold months.
grow taller during the winter.
save water during the winter.
explanation: Leaves lose water, and frozen ground makes water hard to get, so dropping them saves water. Without leaves, trees catch less sunlight, not more.

An art historian noticed that a painting signed by a famous seventeenth-century artist used a blue pigment that was not invented until the 1700s. If her identification of the pigment is correct, the painting ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: must have been painted earlier than any of the artist's other known works.
was painted in the seventeenth century using only older pigments.
proves that the artist invented the blue pigment before anyone else.
could not have been painted entirely by that artist in the seventeenth century.
explanation: A pigment from the 1700s cannot appear in a work completed earlier, so at least part was painted later. The 'only older pigments' option contradicts the pigment found.

In a study, people who were told that a wine cost a lot rated it as tasting better than people who were told the same wine was cheap. The wine in both cases was identical. This suggests that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: what people expect can shape how they judge taste.
price has no effect on how people judge food or drink.
expensive wines always taste better than cheaper ones.
the two groups of people were served two different wines.
explanation: The wine was identical, so the different ratings came from the stated price. The two-wines option contradicts 'The wine in both cases was identical'.

Records show that a town's ice-cream sales and its number of drowning accidents both rise in summer. A newspaper suggested that eating ice cream makes swimming dangerous. A more likely explanation is that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: hot weather leads both to more ice-cream eating and to more swimming.
ice cream makes swimmers too heavy to stay afloat in the water.
drowning accidents cause people in the town to buy more ice cream.
people in the town swim only in the winter months of each year.
explanation: Summer heat raises both ice-cream sales and swimming, and more swimming means more drownings, so the two rise together without one causing the other. Reversing the cause, as the first wrong option does, still treats a shared pattern as cause and effect.

Seagulls often follow fishing boats back to harbour. As the crew clean their catch, they throw unwanted fish parts into the water. The gulls follow the boats most likely because ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: they are trained by the fishermen.
they are trying to escape from bad weather far out at sea.
they can find easy food near the boats.
they nest on the boats at night.
explanation: The crew throw fish parts overboard, giving gulls an easy meal. Nothing suggests training, storms or nesting.

A company tested two versions of an email asking customers to renew their subscriptions. The first email listed the service's features; the second added a line saying how many neighbours in the customer's city had renewed. The second email led to more renewals. This suggests that customers ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: preferred long lists of features to any information about others.
were offered a lower price in the second email than in the first.
did not read either of the emails that the company sent to them.
were influenced by knowing what people near them had done.
explanation: The only added element was the neighbours line, and renewals rose. A lower price is not mentioned; it would be a different change.

Fossils of sea shells have been found high in the mountains of northern Pakistan, thousands of metres above sea level. Shells like these form only in the sea. The rock containing them must therefore ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: once have lain under the sea before being lifted up.
be much younger than the shells that it contains.
have formed at the top of the mountains in fresh water.
have been carried up the mountains by people long ago.
explanation: Sea shells form only in the sea, so the rock was once under the sea and was later raised. Fresh-water formation contradicts 'only in the sea'.

Mariam's houseplant began drooping when she went away for two weeks and no one watered it. After she watered it, the plant stood up straight again within a day. The drooping was probably caused by ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: a disease spreading through its leaves and stems.
the cold weather outside.
too much sunlight in the room.
a lack of water.
explanation: The plant drooped when unwatered and recovered quickly when watered. A disease would not clear up within a day of watering.

Surveys show that people who drink green tea live longer, on average, than people who do not. However, the green-tea drinkers in these surveys were also more likely to exercise, avoid smoking and eat more vegetables. From these surveys alone, researchers cannot conclude that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: people who avoid smoking are included in the surveys.
the green-tea drinkers in the surveys exercised more than others.
green tea itself is the reason the drinkers lived longer.
the green-tea drinkers lived longer, on average, than non-drinkers.
explanation: Exercise, not smoking and diet are rival explanations, so green tea's own effect is uncertain. The other options restate facts the surveys did report.

A village in Thar installed a solar-powered pump to raise water from a deep well. Before the pump, women and girls spent hours each day carrying water. A year later, teachers reported that more girls were attending school regularly. A likely explanation is that the pump ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: made the school building larger and more comfortable.
replaced the village school's need for any teachers at all.
freed time that girls had once spent fetching water.
made the water in the well deeper and harder to reach.
explanation: Girls once spent hours carrying water; with the pump that time could go to school. The pump has nothing to do with the school building.
